name: Fish Sayadieh with Caramelised Onions and Tahini Sauce

components.name: Spiced Fish
steps: Season 900 g fish with measured salt, pepper and cumin. Heat 18 ml oil in a separate skillet and cook fillets gently on both sides to 63 C.
Portion onion rice and fish, adding reserved onions and nuts. Store tahini sauce in a separate chilled container.

components.name: Spiced Onion Rice
steps: Slice 440 g onions and cook slowly in 35 ml oil until deeply golden; set aside one quarter for topping.
Add rice, cumin and cinnamon to the onion pot and stir to coat. Pour in 760 ml hot fish stock, cover and simmer until rice is cooked; rest off heat.

components.name: Tahini Sauce & Topping
steps: Whisk 100 g tahini, 80 ml lemon juice and 80 ml cold water until smooth and pourable.
Toast 35 g pine nuts in a dry pan. Flake the fish into large chunks, avoiding small bones.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Published source uses fish with head for homemade stock. Adaptation uses fillets and shop-bought fish stock; 5 fixed servings for meal scale.
Storing & reheating: Fish and onion rice can freeze well with texture changes. Prepare tahini sauce separately and refrigerate 2-3 days, not frozen.
Freezer: fish and rice; sauce separately

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish to 63°C, shrimp and shellfish until opaque and firm (mussels must open), and reheat to at least 74°C.

flags.shelfLife: Fish — plan for days 1-3; freeze later-week portions. Tahini sauce keeps 2-3 days, not frozen.

foodSafety: Refrigerate perishables promptly in shallow containers: within 2 hours after cooking, or within 1 hour if the air temperature is above 32 C.
Store at 4 C or colder. General cooked-leftover limit: 3-4 days; for delicate seafood recipes follow any shorter specific limit above.
Freeze later-week portions promptly, if this recipe is flagged freezer-suitable; thaw in refrigerator, not on a kitchen counter.
For fish, target a safe cooked internal temperature of 63 C; shrimp and shellfish should be cooked until opaque / firm, and mussels must open during cooking.
Reheat leftovers thoroughly to 74 C, avoiding repeated reheating and cooling cycles.
Cooked rice requires rapid chilling, appropriate cold storage and thorough reheating. Rice left warm for a prolonged period is not made safe by reheating.
Shellfish, fish, soy, dairy, wheat, egg, nuts and pork vary by recipe; verify allergens and dietary restrictions before importing.
